You are an autonomous software engineer working in this repository. You follow a structured engineering workflow.

## Task
Fix the issue described in ISSUE.md.

## Workflow

RECONNAISSANCE → DIAGNOSIS → INVESTIGATION → IMPLEMENTATION → VERIFICATION → FINALIZATION

You will be guided phase-by-phase via system prompts. Do not skip phases.

### RECONNAISSANCE
Inspect repository structure before changing code: package.json, source files, tests, config, relevant documentation. Use read/grep/bash/ls. Do not edit yet. Findings are tracked via evidence.

### DIAGNOSIS
Form explicit hypotheses. Each hypothesis needs: description, supporting evidence, confidence, relevant files.
Track hypotheses via file `.v1/state.json`:
- Read `.v1/state.json` first
- Add hypothesis: `node .v1/helpers.js add-hypothesis '{"description":"...","evidence":["file:line"],"confidence":0.8,"files":["src/foo.ts"]}'`
- Select one: `node .v1/helpers.js select-hypothesis <id>`
You must have at least one hypothesis with evidence before advancing.

### INVESTIGATION
Gather evidence to validate/reject your hypothesis. You may: inspect code, run tests, create a minimal reproduction under `.v1/` or /tmp (do NOT rely on any hidden benchmark harness), inspect call paths. Record command results as evidence. Keep scratch files under `.v1/` so they are not included in the final patch.

### IMPLEMENTATION
Modify the repository only after selecting a diagnosis. Keep changes minimal and focused on the selected hypothesis. Avoid unrelated refactors.

### VERIFICATION
Gather evidence your fix works. Run: relevant existing tests (vitest), your reproduction script, type checks if applicable. You must execute a verification command and observe its result — do not claim success without execution evidence.
If verification fails, you will loop back to investigation/implementation (max 5 iterations).

### FINALIZATION
Before finishing: inspect final diff (`git diff HEAD --stat`, `git diff HEAD` excluding .v1/), ensure change is focused, report verification evidence, then stop.

## Constraints
- Do NOT attempt to read hidden evaluator files or benchmark internals beyond the provided workspace (only `ISSUE.md` and the repository are provided).
- The hidden evaluation oracle is not available; you must discover your own verification strategy.
- Use tools: read, bash, edit, write, grep, find, ls.
- Keep scratchpad files under `.v1/` or /tmp — they will be excluded from the patch.
- Hypotheses must be tracked via `.v1/state.json` or `node .v1/helpers.js` (file-based, not just in chat).

## Reporting
Before termination, summarize: root cause, selected hypothesis, files changed, verification commands run and their results.

## Reconnaissance Summary

**Repository:** A task management library with:
- `src/task-manager.ts` - Core TaskManager class
- `src/types.ts` - Type definitions for Task, CreateTaskInput, UpdateTaskInput
- `src/validators.ts` - Validation functions
- `src/utils.ts` - Utility functions
- `tests/task-manager.test.ts` - Tests for TaskManager

**The Bug:**
In `src/task-manager.ts`, the `updateTask` method has a bug at lines 33-40:

```typescript
// BUG: spreads undefined values and overwrites existing fields
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,
  description: updates.description as any,
  priority: updates.priority as any,
  status: updates.status as any,
  dueDate: updates.dueDate as any,
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

The problem is that when you do:
```js
{ ...existing, title: updates.title }
```
If `updates.title` is `undefined`, it overwrites `existing.title` with `undefined`.

In JavaScript, object spread with an explicitly undefined value will overwrite the existing value:
```js
const obj = { a: 1, b: 2 };
const result = { ...obj, a: undefined };
// result = { a: undefined, b: 2 }  ← a is now undefined, not 1
```

**The Fix:**
Only assign fields that are actually provided (not undefined). We can use conditional spread or nullish coalescing to handle this properly.

## Reconnaissance Summary

**Repository:** A task management library with:
- `src/task-manager.ts` - Core TaskManager class

- `src/utils.ts` - Utility functions
- `tests/task-manager.test.ts` - Tests for TaskManager

**The Bug:**
In `src/task-manager.ts`, the `updateTask` method has a bug at lines 33-40:

```typescript
// BUG: spreads undefined values and overwrites existing fields
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,
  description: updates.description as any,
  priority: updates.priority as any,
  status: updates.status as any,
  dueDate: updates.dueDate as any,
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

The problem is that when you do:
```js
{ ...existing, title: updates.title }
```
If `updates.title` is `undefined`, it overwrites `existing.title` with `undefined`.

In JavaScript, object spread with an explicitly undefined value will overwrite the existing value:
```js
const obj = { a: 1, b: 2 };
const result = { ...obj, a: undefined };
// result = { a: undefined, b: 2 }  ← a is now undefined, not 1
```

**The Fix:**
Only assign fields that are actually provided (not undefined). We can use conditional spread or nullish coalescing to handle this properly.

Now I have a complete understanding of the issue and the codebase. Let me summarize my findings:

## Reconnaissance Summary

**Repository:** A task management library with:
- `src/task-manager.ts` - Core TaskManager class
- `src/types.ts` - Type definitions for Task, CreateTaskInput, UpdateTaskInput
- `src/validators.ts` - Validation functions
- `src/utils.ts` - Utility functions
- `tests/task-manager.test.ts` - Tests for TaskManager

**The Bug:**
In `src/task-manager.ts`, the `updateTask` method has a bug at lines 33-40:

```typescript
// BUG: spreads undefined values and overwrites existing fields
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,
  description: updates.description as any,
  priority: updates.priority as any,
  status: updates.status as any,
  dueDate: updates.dueDate as any,
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

The problem is that when you do:
```js
{ ...existing, title: updates.title }
```
If `updates.title` is `undefined`, it overwrites `existing.title` with `undefined`.

In JavaScript, object spread with an explicitly undefined value will overwrite the existing value:
```js
const obj = { a: 1, b: 2 };
const result = { ...obj, a: undefined };
// result = { a: undefined, b: 2 }  ← a is now undefined, not 1
```

**The Fix:**
Only assign fields that are actually provided (not undefined). We can use conditional spread or nullish coalescing to handle this properly.

Now I have a complete understanding of the issue and the codebase. Let me summarize my findings:

## Reconnaissance Summary

**Repository:** A task management library with:
- `src/task-manager.ts` - Core TaskManager class
- `src/types.ts` - Type definitions for Task, CreateTaskInput, UpdateTaskInput
- `src/validators.ts` - Validation functions
- `src/utils.ts` - Utility functions
- `tests/task-manager.test.ts` - Tests for TaskManager

**The Bug:**
In `src/task-manager.ts`, the `updateTask` method has a bug at lines 33-40:

```typescript
// BUG: spreads undefined values and overwrites existing fields
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,
  description: updates.description as any,
  priority: updates.priority as any,
  status: updates.status as any,
  dueDate: updates.dueDate as any,
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

The problem is that when you do:
```js
{ ...existing, title: updates.title }
```
If `updates.title` is `undefined`, it overwrites `existing.title` with `undefined`.

In JavaScript, object spread with an explicitly undefined value will overwrite the existing value:
```js
const obj = { a: 1, b: 2 };
const result = { ...obj, a: undefined };
// result = { a: undefined, b: 2 }  ← a is now undefined, not 1
```

**The Fix:**
Only assign fields that are actually provided (not undefined). We can use conditional spread or nullish coalescing to handle this properly.

  dueDate: updates.dueDate as any,
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};

When `updates.title` is `undefined`, the spread `{ ...existing, title: undefined }` results in `title: undefined`, overwriting the existing value.

The fix is to conditionally include fields only when they are not undefined. I can use the pattern:
```typescript

  ...existing,
  ...(updates.title !== undefined && { title: updates.title.trim() }),

  ...(updates.status !== undefined && { status: updates.status }),
  ...(updates.dueDate !== undefined && { dueDate: updates.dueDate }),
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

Or use a cleaner approach with Object.assign or building the update object incrementally.

## Summary

**Root Cause:** The `updateTask` method in `src/task-manager.ts` was explicitly assigning update fields without checking if they were undefined. In JavaScript, `{ ...existing, title: undefined }` results in `title: undefined`, overwriting the existing value.

**Selected Hypothesis:** hyp-1 - The updateTask method explicitly assigns update fields without checking if they are undefined, causing undefined values to overwrite existing fields.

**Files Changed:**
- `src/task-manager.ts` - Changed the `updateTask` method to use conditional spread (`...(updates.field !== undefined && { field: value })`) so only explicitly provided fields are updated.

**Verification Evidence:**
1. Created `.v1/repro.ts` to reproduce the bug - confirmed bug existed (all fields were erased)
2. After fix, repro.ts passes: "All fields preserved correctly!"
3. All 11 existing tests pass: `npx vitest run` → 11 passed

The fix is minimal and focused on the issue - only the `updateTask` method was modified.

In `src/task-manager.ts`, the `updateTask` method at lines 33-40:
```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,
  description: updates.description as any,
  priority: updates.priority as any,
  status: updates.status as any,
  dueDate: updates.dueDate as any,
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

When `updates.title` is `undefined`, the spread `{ ...existing, title: undefined }` results in `title: undefined`, overwriting the existing value.

The fix is to conditionally include fields only when they are not undefined. I can use the pattern:
```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  ...(updates.title !== undefined && { title: updates.title.trim() }),
  ...(updates.description !== undefined && { description: updates.description }),
  ...(updates.priority !== undefined && { priority: updates.priority }),
  ...(updates.status !== undefined && { status: updates.status }),
  ...(updates.dueDate !== undefined && { dueDate: updates.dueDate }),
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

Or use a cleaner approach with Object.assign or building the update object incrementally.

Now let me implement the fix. The bug is in `src/task-manager.ts` at the `updateTask` method. The issue is that when assigning:
```typescript
title: updates.title as any,
```
If `updates.title` is `undefined`, it overwrites the existing value.

The fix is to only include properties that are not undefined. I can use conditional spread patterns:
```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  ...(updates.title !== undefined && { title: updates.title.trim() }),
  ...(updates.description !== undefined && { description: updates.description }),
  ...(updates.priority !== undefined && { priority: updates.priority }),
  ...(updates.status !== undefined && { status: updates.status }),
  ...(updates.dueDate !== undefined && { dueDate: updates.dueDate }),
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

But I also need to be careful about the title trimming - when title is provided, it should be trimmed. Let me implement this fix.

## Finalization Summary

### Root Cause
The `updateTask` method in `src/task-manager.ts` was explicitly assigning update fields (`title`, `description`, `priority`, `status`, `dueDate`) without checking if they were undefined. In JavaScript, spreading an object with an explicitly undefined value (`{ ...existing, title: undefined }`) results in `title: undefined`, overwriting the existing value instead of preserving it.

### Selected Hypothesis
**hyp-101c6657**: The `updateTask` method explicitly assigns each update field without checking if it is undefined. In JavaScript, spreading an object with an explicitly undefined value overwrites the existing value instead of preserving it.

### Files Changed
- **`src/task-manager.ts`** - Modified the `updateTask` method to use conditional spread (`...(updates.field !== undefined && { field: value })`) so only explicitly provided fields are updated.

### Verification Commands Run
1. **`npx vitest run`** - All 11 tests passed ✅
2. **`npx tsx .v1/repro.ts`** - "All fields preserved correctly!" ✅

### The Fix
Changed from:
```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,
  description: updates.description as any,
  // ... etc
};
```

To:
```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  ...(updates.title !== undefined && { title: updates.title.trim() }),
  ...(updates.description !== undefined && { description: updates.description }),
  // ... etc
};
```

This ensures only fields that are explicitly provided (not undefined) are updated, preserving all other existing field values.

## Finalization Summary

### Root Cause
The `updateTask` method in `src/task-manager.ts` was explicitly assigning update fields (`title`, `description`, `priority`, `status`, `dueDate`) without checking if they were undefined. In JavaScript, spreading an object with an explicitly undefined value (`{ ...existing, title: undefined }`) results in `title: undefined`, overwriting the existing value instead of preserving it.

### Selected Hypothesis
**hyp-101c6657**: The `updateTask` method explicitly assigns each update field without checking if it is undefined. In JavaScript, spreading an object with an explicitly undefined value overwrites the existing value instead of preserving it.

### Files Changed
- **`src/task-manager.ts`** - Modified the `updateTask` method to use conditional spread (`...(updates.field !== undefined && { field: value })`) so only explicitly provided fields are updated.

### Verification Commands Run
1. **`npx vitest run`** - All 11 tests passed ✅
2. **`npx tsx .v1/repro.ts`** - "All fields preserved correctly!" ✅

### The Fix
Changed from:
```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,
  description: updates.description as any,
  // ... etc
};
```

To:
```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  ...(updates.title !== undefined && { title: updates.title.trim() }),
  ...(updates.description !== undefined && { description: updates.description }),
  // ... etc
};
```

This ensures only fields that are explicitly provided (not undefined) are updated, preserving all other existing field values.

content.text:
## Finalization Summary

### Root Cause
The `updateTask` method in `src/task-manager.ts` was explicitly assigning update fields (`title`, `description`, `priority`, `status`, `dueDate`) without checking if they were undefined. In JavaScript, spreading an object with an explicitly undefined value (`{ ...existing, title: undefined }`) results in `title: undefined`, overwriting the existing value instead of preserving it.

### Selected Hypothesis
**hyp-101c6657**: The `updateTask` method explicitly assigns each update field without checking if it is undefined. In JavaScript, spreading an object with an explicitly undefined value overwrites the existing value instead of preserving it.

### Files Changed
- **`src/task-manager.ts`** - Modified the `updateTask` method to use conditional spread (`...(updates.field !== undefined && { field: value })`) so only explicitly provided fields are updated.

### Verification Commands Run
1. **`npx vitest run`** - All 11 tests passed ✅
2. **`npx tsx .v1/repro.ts`** - "All fields preserved correctly!" ✅

### The Fix
Changed from:
```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,
  description: updates.description as any,
  // ... etc
};
```

To:
```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  ...(updates.title !== undefined && { title: updates.title.trim() }),
  ...(updates.description !== undefined && { description: updates.description }),
  // ... etc
};
```

This ensures only fields that are explicitly provided (not undefined) are updated, preserving all other existing field values.

## Investigation Evidence Summary

### Hypothesis Confirmed ✅

**Hypothesis:** The `updateTask` method explicitly assigns each update field without checking if it is undefined, causing undefined values to overwrite existing fields.

**Evidence gathered:**

| Evidence | Result |
|----------|--------|
| **Reproduction script** (`.v1/repro.ts`) | ✅ "All fields preserved correctly!" |
| **Existing tests** (`npx vitest run`) | ✅ 11/11 tests passed |
| **Code diff** (`git diff HEAD`) | ✅ Fix in place using conditional spread |

### Fix Applied

**Before (buggy):**
```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,      // overwrites with undefined
  description: updates.description as any,
  // ...
};
```

**After (fixed):**
```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  ...(updates.title !== undefined && { title: updates.title.trim() }),
  ...(updates.description !== undefined && { description: updates.description }),
  // ...
};
```

The conditional spread pattern (`...(condition && { field: value })`) ensures that when a field is `undefined` in the updates, the spread evaluates to `false` and produces an empty object, preserving the existing value from `...existing`.
